title: Suspect Calls 911 on Himself Then Drives at Police With Gun Drawn
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Sparks, Nevada — On March 12th, 2026, at approximately 11:31 a.m., Sparks Police Dispatch received a 911 call from a subject advising he was going to enter an occupied local business in the 600 block of North McCarran Boulevard in the Silver State Plaza and quote, "Shoot Everybody in The Business." The subject told dispatch that he was in a white Chevrolet S10 pickup in the parking lot and that he had a handgun with him. While officers were responding, a Sparks Police crisis negotiator contacted the subject via phone. The negotiator made 13 additional attempts to recontact the subject, but was unsuccessful. Officers arrived in the area at approximately 11:38 a.m. Once on scene, they immediately contacted the business to ensure the safety of the people inside. As additional resources arrived, a Sparks Police drone was used to assist in locating the subject. 

Officers also attempted to utilize an emergency ping to pinpoint the subject's location through his cell phone. At approximately 11:50 a.m., officers located a vehicle matching the description given by the subject during his 911 call. The subject's vehicle was in the parking lot west of the business. Officers did not approach the vehicle initially, but watched it from a distance while waiting for additional resources to arrive. While officers continued to attempt phone contact with the subject and monitor his vehicle, a Sparks Police armored vehicle was requested to respond to help increase the safety of officers on scene. At approximately 11:54 a.m., officers observed the subject release a dog from inside the truck. Then at approximately 11:56 a.m., the subject drove southbound through the parking lot at a high rate of speed towards marked police vehicles. The subject produced a firearm and pointed it in the direction of the officers. Officers were still inside their vehicles as the subject vehicle drove toward them. 

The subject used his vehicle to strike the driver's side of a canine patrol vehicle, temporarily trapping the officer inside. The subject vehicle continued and struck an unmarked police vehicle head-on. At approximately 11:57 a.m., officers discharged their firearms at the subject who remained inside of his vehicle. Officers remained behind cover at a distance while awaiting the arrival of the armored vehicle. At approximately officers began making announcements over the PA system to encourage the subject to surrender. Announcements were made for approximately 14 minutes and no response was received from the subject. At approximately 12:13 p.m., officers approached the vehicle and located the subject inside. On-seen medical personnel immediately began rendering aid. However, the subject was later pronounced deceased on scene. The suspect was later identified as 39-year-old Jedidiah Guerra. The investigation revealed that Guerrero was in possession of a black handgun at the time of the incident.
